Output 1: 1.1 The Lab utilized 7 new data sources in 2022.
Primary Data: 1) Surveys, 2) Micro-surveys 3) Interviews 4) Focus groups 5) Workshop Systematizations,
Secondary Data: 6) Official Statistical Data, 7) Government Reports
1.2 The Lab used 13 different types of data in 2022.
1) Crowd source 2) Citizen-generated data 3) Direct interviews 4) Ecosystem mapping 5) Experiments 6) Focus group 7) Issue mapping 8) Literature review and grey documents analysis 9) Participatory observation 10) Qualitative interviews 11) Socioeconomic data 12) Surveys 13) User journeys
1.3 25 new solutions were mapped on the solutions mapping platform in 2022
1.4 The Lab utilized at least 8 innovation methods in its different learning loops in 2022: 1) Co-creation 2) Collective Intelligence 3) Design Thinking 4) Ethnography 5) Sensemaking 6) Solutions Mapping 7) Pilots 8) Prototyping
Output 2: 2.1 24 blogs and substantial media posts in 2022.
2.2 Public sector institutions were key partners in each of the Laboratory’s portfolios and learning loops during 2022 the lab.
Public and Social Innovation:
1) Developed and implemented a 14-week innovation-methods training course for teams from 11 different government ministries, in collaboration with the National Innovation Strategy (ENI) and the National Science and Technology Council (CONACYT). 2) Implemented public service digitalization pilot projects developed as part of the ENI/CONACYT training course by the Ministry of Labor and the Social Cabinet of the Presidency. 3) Designed and implemented a community innovation challenge, Moiru (2022), focused on decent work, economic growth, and gender equality, with the National University of Itapúa.
Enterprise and Employment Formalization: 4) Designed, implemented, and disseminated the findings of a garment workshop census with the Municipality of Yaguaron. 5) Designed and implemented a methodology for mapping the needs, demands, and available support from SMEs, including a survey of 450 SMEs in two territories, in collaboration with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and the local Entrepreneur Support Centers in two municipalities.
Participatory Governance: 6) Designed and implemented, Tavarandu, a program to build local capacities for participatory governance and innovation, with participation of teams of officials from 12 municipalities in the training course, and representatives of 2 municipalities participating in citizens’ laboratories.
2.3
1) The National Innovation Strategy (ENI) has integrated human centered design methods and principles into its public innovators’ program based on continued interaction and advising with the AccLab in Paraguay.
2) The Center for Innovation in Family Agriculture (CIAF) at the National University of Asunción utilized collective intelligence and sensemaking methodologies for a Territorial Forum held in 2022. They have expressed great interest in adopting, wholescale, the Acclab’s learning loop methodology and receiving continued support and advising to develop their research agenda and portfolio of participatory action-learning projects.
2.4 Each of the lab’s learning and experiment portfolios has made substantial and actionable contributions to the work of ongoing and new projects in the Country Office during 2022:
CO Inclusive Growth Portfolio 1) The AccLab’s impact assessment of the 2021 initiative, My Neighborhood Without Waste , has been integrated into the design of the second installment of the program, developed and implemented during 2022 as part of the Solid Waste Management component of the CO project, “Asuncion Green City of the Americas”.
2) The AccLab’s experience conducting sensemaking exercises and constructing learning and experimentation portfolios served as a basis for the successful Portfolio Initiation Framework exercise carried out by the Paraguay CO to develop a proposal for a portfolio focused on Sustainable Finance, Improved Data Management, and Coordinated Interinstitutional Governance for meeting the Nationally Determined Contributions for greenhouse gas emissions reduction.
CO Environment and Sustainable Development Portfolio 3) The AccLab’s prior experience designing and implementing the Participatory Employment Formalization Laboratory and related learning loops on work and informal employment in the construction, domestic work, apparel, and recycling industries served as a basis for developing a proposal for an “SME Formalization and Promotion Portfolio”, successfully submitted to the UNDP Poverty and Inequality Funding Window. This project will be implemented in collaboration with the CO’s Inclusive Growth Portfolio in 2022.
CO Governance Portfolio 4) The AccLab’s expertise and prior work on participatory governance methodologies supported a successful proposal for the TRAC-funding call for “Maximizing the Strategic Plan Enablers in Latin America”. Currently the lab is implementing, Tavarandu, a program to build local capacities for participatory governance and innovation and develop digital tools for local citizen participation, in collaboration with the CO Governance Portfolio.
Output 3: 3.1 The lab participates in the weekly Drop-In calls and biweekly calls by role (solution mappers, explorers, and experimenters), in addition to ad hoc meetings with individual labs and the chats on teams and whatsapp.
3.2 The lab disseminates its blog publications to other labs through Microsoft Teams and the three Whatsapp chat groups (Solution Mappers, Explorers, and Experimenters) as well as the Latin America Regional Labs Whatsapp group. These provide a continuous summary of the methodological insights and sustainable development learning generated by our activities.
3.3 The AccLab activities are shared through the CO social networks (twitter, facebook, instagram and linkedin) with a minimum monthly frequency, the content includes: blogs, workshops and field activities, calls, and results presentations tagging allied institutions and organizations. An average of 5 posts per month were published in 2022:
3.4 12 social media profiles engaged through collaborative dissemination of activities and findings including the Ministry of Labor, Fundación Paraguaya, the Municipality of Yaguarón, CEAMSO, Alma Cívica, GirlsCode, the National University of Itapúa, Reacción, Mathematics Olympics of Paraguay, Autonomous University of Encarnacion, Mi Barrio sin Residuos, and Cultura y Participacion.

The AccLab colaborated in the contest and proposal workshops design and the implementation of the winning proposal. 4) During 2020, face-to-face and virtual training was carried out for the entire CO on: solution mapping, hypothesis design, collective intelligence and human-centered design.
